headline: High: Mentat can write and modify shared files while the paired repo-list agent is non-runnable, so the main risks are file-based conflict and downstream misuse of its outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot ingest B’s outputs by default. Profile B reads and writes files and uses stdin/stdout, so manual copy-paste or file handoff could bridge them, but that is an unusual configuration and the blast radius is limited to text content.
conditions: IF an operator copies B’s output into A-maintained notes or prompts, then prompt injection becomes possible.
IF A is wrapped in a separate parser that treats B-generated text as instructions, then the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A as a static reference list with no ingestion path.
Do not paste B output into any agent prompt without review.
Use a plain-text separator when transferring snippets.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to any shared text pipeline.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no I/O, while B only touches source code in selected files and can read/write the filesystem. The pair does not show a shared sensitive-data class or automatic upload path, so leakage is limited unless operators place secrets in the shared workspace.
conditions: IF secrets or regulated data are stored in files that B can read, then B may expose them through its model-provider calls.
IF A is used as a repository of sensitive notes, then B can read them from the shared filesystem.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Restrict B to a dedicated project directory.
Rotate any API keys that appear in editable files.
Review file lists before launching B.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or runtime capabilities, but B can write the filesystem and modify git state, with shared state explicitly via filesystem. That creates a default write-conflict pathway if multiple B instances or other tools touch the same repo; A is not a writer, so it is not the source of conflict but is part of the pairwise environment.
conditions: IF two B instances operate on the same checkout, then file and git conflicts can occur.
IF another tool edits the same directory while B is running, then last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Run only one B instance per checkout.
Use separate working directories.
Commit or stash before starting B.
Check git status before applying diffs.
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared workspaces.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a static reference source, while B produces diff-based edit proposals and coordinates multi-file edits. If operators treat A’s curated list or B’s generated edits as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect code changes. A does not act, but B can operationalize mistaken inputs from the pairwise workflow.
conditions: IF B’s proposed diffs are applied without human review, then incorrect edits can propagate.
IF A’s repository metadata is used as a factual source for automation, then stale or misleading references can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review before applying diffs.
Cross-check A’s references against primary sources.
Limit B to small patch sets.
Record the source of each accepted change.
requires-engineering: add automated validation tests before merge.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source repository with no touched data classes, while B handles source code and model-provider API keys. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced, so compliance risk is mainly local handling of secrets in B rather than a pairwise breach. A is not cited for a residency issue because none is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B’s editable files, then retention and logging policies may matter.
IF model-provider logs retain prompts containing secrets, then compliance obligations may be triggered.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in the workspace.
Remove secrets from files before editing.
Confirm provider logging settings.
Use a separate repo for sensitive work.
requires-engineering: document retention and deletion procedures.
